title: Business Central 2026 release wave 2 (BC29): Faster data loading with improved data model for table extensions (all fields on an AL table are stored in the same table)
summary: Business Central 2026 wave 2 (BC29) consolidates all table extension fields into a single physical database table instead of companion tables, eliminating SQL JOINs and improving database operation performance across the system.
key_points: BC23 put all extension fields into one companion table ($ext) per base table, so queries needed at most one SQL join.
In BC29 the companion table is gone. Fields from table extensions are stored in the base table itself, so no joins are needed.
Adding more table extensions adds columns, not tables. The columns keep the FieldName$ExtensionID naming.
The AL table model does not change, so extension publishers do not need to change any code.

quotes.text: No matter how many extensions and table extensions you have, in the actual database, there will always be only one table.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies the fundamental architectural change and its scalability advantage

quotes.text: This change does not impact the table model as seen from the AL language, so no code changes are needed from extension/app publishers.
quotes.why_it_matters: Key insight that backward compatibility is maintained despite significant internal changes
